subject: Error in exists(name, env) : argument "env" is missing, with no default

messages.author: fdc3837978b1392b
messages.subject: Error in exists(name, env) : argument "env" is missing, with no default
parts:
Dear all,

I'm trying to make a simple barplot using geom_bar


c <-ggplot(DataMain0.2, aes(factor(DataMain0.2$TAC)), y = DataMain0.2$lr) 

c + geom_bar(stat="identity")

I get the following error message and I have no idea how to work around that problem.

Error in exists(name, env) : argument "env" is missing, with no default

Any comments are appreciated!

Rasmus

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Error in exists(name, env) : argument "env" is missing, with no default
parts:
On Fri, Jul 4, 2014 at 6:48 AM, rbruckner <rasmusb...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Dear all,
>
> I'm trying to make a simple barplot using geom_bar
>
>
> c <-ggplot(DataMain0.2, aes(factor(DataMain0.2$TAC)), y = DataMain0.2$lr)

Try this instead:

ggplot(DataMain0.2, aes(x = factor(TAC), y = lr)) +
geom_bar(stat="identity")

You want to map TAC to x and lr to y, so you need both inside the
aes() call. Secondly, since the data frame is named in the first
argument of ggplot(), you don't need to use it again inside aes().

Dennis
